title: Fixes #36118: Keep entities without a name when the filter pattern is empty

files.patch:
@@ -51,11 +51,11 @@ def _filter(filter_pattern: FilterPattern | None, name: str | None) -> bool:
     :param name: table or schema name
     :return: True for filtering, False otherwise
     """
-    if not filter_pattern:
-        # No filter pattern, nothing to filter
+    if filter_pattern is None or not filter_pattern_enabled(filter_pattern):
+        # No filter pattern, or one without includes/excludes: nothing to filter
         return False
 
-    if filter_pattern and not name:
+    if not name:
         # Filter pattern is present but not the name so we'll filter it out
         return True

@@ -23,6 +23,7 @@
     filter_by_classifications,
     filter_by_dashboard,
     filter_by_fqn,
+    filter_by_project,
     filter_pattern_enabled,
     validate_regex,
 )
@@ -47,6 +48,19 @@ def test_filter():
     assert _filter(filter_pattern_both, "potato_tomato")
 
 
+def test_filter_without_configured_pattern_keeps_nameless_entities():
+    """An empty pattern filters nothing, also when the entity has no name"""
+    assert not _filter(None, None)
+    # What the UI saves for "scan all": a pattern with empty includes and excludes
+    assert not _filter(FilterPattern(includes=[], excludes=[]), None)
+    assert not _filter(FilterPattern(), None)
+    assert not _filter(FilterPattern(), "potato")
+    # A real pattern still filters out an entity without a name
+    assert _filter(FilterPattern(includes=["^potato$"]), None)
+    assert _filter(FilterPattern(excludes=["^tomato$"]), "")
+    assert not filter_by_project(FilterPattern(includes=[], excludes=[]), None)
+
+
 def test_filter_server_compatible_no_pattern_keeps_everything():
     assert _filter_server_compatible(None, "anything") is False
     assert _filter_server_compatible(FilterPattern(), "anything") is False
